title: Inference cost guidance by interaction patterns
content:
Purpose:
This doc synthesizes a set of pragmatic recommendation heuristics for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization that map directly to cells in our cost-model spreadsheet. The focus is to make repeatable, simulation-driven recommendations for three canonical interaction patterns (short single-shot prompts, multi-turn chat, and long completion workloads) so PM/Eng/SRE can quickly pick a configuration and estimate cost/quality tradeoffs in the sheet.

Context and goals:
- Context: customers are running heterogeneous workloads; our existing optimize docs provide many presets but rarely tie back cleanly to interaction shape. Engineering needs quick rules-of-thumb and a short checklist to run a cost sweep.
- Goals: provide recommended default settings per interaction pattern, show how those settings change the model of cost in the linked spreadsheet, and provide an easy simulation plan to validate on staging.

Interaction patterns and recommended defaults (high-level):
1) Short single-shot prompts (median prompt length 20-80 tokens; completion 20-200 tokens)
   - Latency SLO: 100-300ms P95 (interactive UI)
   - Batching: small, tight windows (batch window 5-15ms); target batch size 2-8 depending on traffic; enable continuous batching with max_batch_size set to 16 for peaks.
   - Caching: strong prefix caching for repeated prompts; TTL 5-30 minutes for deterministic prompts (e.g., product description templates), 1-5 minutes for dynamic but repeated queries. Cache key: SHA(prefix_tokens + prompt_template_id). Cache hit guidance: prioritize prefix cache over KV cache for short prompts.
   - Quantization: prefer 8-bit (int8 or dynamic 8-bit) for small-medium models (<30B) to get cost wins with minimal quality risk. For larger models (>30B) evaluate 4-bit QAT/LLM.int4 only after running quality sweep.
   - Cost model cells to edit: 'batch_window_ms', 'target_batch_size', 'cache_hit_rate_short', 'quant_mode_short'.

2) Multi-turn chat (average turn 40-120 tokens, KV reuse across turns)
   - Latency SLO: 150-500ms P95 for mainstream chat flows; streaming enabled for UX where possible.
   - Batching: prioritize request affinity (sticky sessions) so that continuous batching doesn't merge different conversations in a way that impacts KV reuse. Configure affinity-based bins and smaller batch windows (10-50ms) with max_batch_size 8-12.
   - Caching: aggressive KV cache reuse: keep per-conversation KV cached in memory and persist warm prefixes for 30+ minutes for active sessions. Enable prefix-level caching for system prompts and common user prompts. Cache eviction policy: LRU with size cap sized to the 99th percentile of active tokens.
   - Quantization: models with heavy KV access can suffer from inaccurate attention scaling after aggressive quant; recommend conservative quant (int8) for production chat models; flagged experiments only for int4 with an eval suite.
   - Cost model cells: 'kv_cache_ttl', 'affinity_enabled', 'cache_eviction_size', 'quant_mode_chat', 'streaming_enabled'.

3) Long completion / generation (single long output, e.g., 1k+ tokens)
   - Latency SLO: larger tail tolerated for batch jobs; P95 targets 1-5s depending on use case.
   - Batching: optimize for token throughput, not request latency. Use larger batch windows (50-200ms) and high max_batch_size (64-256) depending on GPU memory and model KV size. Consider token-aggregation batching if many concurrent long outputs.
   - Caching: prefix caching less effective for long, unique prompts. Instead, enable model-level warm caches (kernel preloads, compiled kernels) and reuse KV where prefix overlap exists. Keep small prefix cache (TTL 1-5 min) for templates.
   - Quantization: strong candidate for int4 or 4-bit families if quality tests pass. Prioritize mixed-precision strategies: keep attention layers higher precision if quality regressions appear.
   - Cost model cells: 'max_batch_size_long', 'batch_window_long_ms', 'quant_mode_long', 'token_aggregation_enabled'.

Guiding heuristics (mapping rules):
- If median completion tokens < 200 and P95 latency target < 300ms -> prioritize small batch windows + prefix cache + int8.
- If median conversation turns > 6 and KV reuse ratio > 0.4 -> prioritize affinity, long KV TTL, conservative quant.
- If median completion tokens > 800 (or > 3x average) -> prioritize throughput batching + aggressive int4 experimentation.

How to use the spreadsheet (quick runbook):
1) Make a copy of the linked cost model spreadsheet (linked_artifacts[0]).
2) Go to the 'interaction-profile' tab and select one of the three profiles (short, chat, long).
3) Edit the highlighted cells: batch_window_ms, target_batch_size, cache_hit_rate, quant_mode. There are comment notes describing realistic ranges; start at the recommended defaults above.
4) Run the sensitivity sheet: change cache_hit_rate +/- 10–30 points and quant discount to see cost delta.
5) Add a quality penalty row if you expect quant to cost savings with a potential quality delta (we track this as a soft multiplier).

Simulation plan for staging (minimal experiments):
- Sweep dimensions: batch_window_ms (5, 25, 100), max_batch_size (8, 64, 128), cache_hit_rate (baseline, baseline+20%), quant_mode (fp16, int8, int4).
- Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, median & P95 latency, GPU utilization, p99 memory pressure, cache hit ratio, end-user quality score (BLEU/ROUGE or human sample score depending on task).
- Run each config for 30 minutes of steady-state traffic; record cost-per-1M-tokens from the runtime. Aggregate into the spreadsheet.

Quality and safety checkpoints before rollout:
- Automated eval: run the model on the 'quant-regression-suite' (existing suite id in linked_artifacts) and require <1.5% quality drop for int8 and <3.0% for int4 for classification/generation metrics unless product approves larger deltas.
- Telemetry checks: add rollout gates to block rollout if p95 latency increases by >25% or if p99 memory exceeds safe margins.
- Operational: ensure tracing tags include batch_id, cache_hit boolean, quant_mode for postmortem.

Edge cases and notes:
- Cold start spikes: smaller batch windows and disabled cache warmups during very low traffic may increase cost; consider burst capacity or a tiny warm pool of idle workers for low-latency guarantees.
- Prompts with high variance: if the same endpoint switches between short and long flows, consider adaptive route policies or separate routes for 'short' vs 'long' to avoid cross-traffic inefficiencies.
- Model families: recommendations above are intentionally conservative—older model families (legacy v1) may not tolerate int8/4 without architecture-specific fixes. Add per-model flags in the spreadsheet.

Deliverables & next steps (owner action items):
- Priya: update the 'interaction-profile' tab in the shared spreadsheet with these defaults and add links to the sweep plan (by 2025-01-17).
- Miguel: implement the minimal staging sweep harness (dimensions above) and push telemetry dashboard (by 2025-01-24).
- Hannah: run quant regression suite and summarize per-model pass/fail matrix (by 2025-01-31).
- Owen: create a short rollout runbook (canary thresholds, abort rules) and attach to the config in the Console (by 2025-02-02).

Open questions for the group:
- What is our conservative default for cache size cap for chat (suggested: 50MB per GPU slot) — is that realistic given memory pressure observed in last cluster test?
- Do we want to expose 'affinity bins' as a user-facing config in Console or keep it as a platform-only knob?
- Should quant quality thresholds be hard-block gates in Dedicated tiers?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally short and prescriptive so PMs and SREs can translate directly into spreadsheet inputs and staging tests. Feedback welcome on ranges and the suggested TTLs — these should reflect realistic cache lifetimes from telemetry.

Appendix: quick cheat sheet (single-line defaults)
- Short prompts: batch_window=10ms, max_batch_size=16, cache_TTL=5m, quant=int8
- Chat: batch_window=30ms, max_batch_size=12, kv_ttl=30m, quant=int8
- Long: batch_window=120ms, max_batch_size=128, kv_ttl=5m, quant=int4 (experiment)
